expectations.text: Forces a single primary outcome rather than measuring all six stated objectives at once
expectations.evidence: "CMX's instruction for SPACES: 'just focus on one objective.' Six objectives on one sheet, six vague sheets nobody refreshes past month two. Pick one now."

expectations.text: Names that primary outcome in the SPACES vocabulary - support, product feedback, acquisition and advocacy, content and contribution, engagement, or success - rather than as an ad-hoc phrase
expectations.evidence: "That's CMX's own SPACES model (Support, Product feedback, Acquisition, Content, Engagement, Success)... Recommendation: Support."

expectations.text: States that every metric on the sheet must plausibly move when that primary outcome moves
expectations.evidence: No explicit statement in section 11 that every metric must plausibly move with the primary outcome; the reasoning given for picking Support is cost/speed of proof, not a stated design rule for the whole sheet

expectations.text: Requires one funnel vocabulary to be chosen and kept - either Orbit's explorer / participant / contributor / advocate ladder or the casual / regular / core split, never both in the same sheet
expectations.evidence: "Use casual/regular/core going forward... Drop Orbit wording from new slides."

expectations.text: States that two vocabularies in one sheet make every cohort definition ambiguous
expectations.evidence: "Skill's rule: one vocabulary, or every cohort definition goes ambiguous."

expectations.text: Notes that the Orbit model is no longer actively developed and cites it as a stable published framework rather than a live standard
expectations.evidence: "Orbit itself is fine to cite as a stable, no-longer-developed reference framework — just not as a second live vocabulary"

expectations.text: Proposes the code-centric starter set: time to first response, change request closure ratio, contributor absence factor and release frequency
expectations.evidence: Change request closure ratio only appears conditionally ("If primary outcome is Content/contribution instead") and release frequency never appears anywhere in the sheet

expectations.text: Adds a recommendability survey item as the fifth starter metric, asked roughly twice a year
expectations.evidence: Recommendability is included but cadence is explicitly "Quarterly 2-item pulse survey" (four times a year), not roughly twice a year

expectations.text: Marks metrics with no prior readings as "baselining" rather than inventing a threshold for them
expectations.evidence: Multiple rows marked e.g. "baselining — pull retention-window history now", "baselining — needs identity map first"

expectations.text: States that at least three prior periods are needed before setting a threshold from the trailing median
expectations.evidence: "> 24h react / > 72h act-now (folklore, unsourced — recalibrate after 3 periods)"

expectations.text: Tracks first-pull-request merge rate and time-to-merge for external contributors separately from maintainers' own pull requests
expectations.evidence: No such metric appears; the closest are "First-time participants per period" and "Second-contribution rate within 90 days (GitHub)", neither of which tracks merge rate or time-to-merge for external vs. maintainer PRs

expectations.text: Forces a single primary outcome rather than measuring all six stated objectives at once
expectations.evidence: The transcript builds a 'six-pillar measurement framework' (support deflection, product feedback, contribution growth, advocacy, retention, general engagement) and the starter scorecard explicitly tracks 'The ⭐ metric from each pillar above, six numbers total' — all six objectives are measured in parallel, no single primary outcome is forced.

expectations.text: Names that primary outcome in the SPACES vocabulary - support, product feedback, acquisition and advocacy, content and contribution, engagement, or success - rather than as an ad-hoc phrase
expectations.evidence: No SPACES vocabulary or any single named primary outcome appears anywhere in the transcript; it uses its own six-pillar taxonomy (support deflection, product feedback, contribution growth, advocacy, retention, general engagement) with no primary outcome selected.

expectations.text: States that every metric on the sheet must plausibly move when that primary outcome moves
expectations.evidence: There is no such requirement stated; the framework instead prescribes one starter metric per pillar independently (section 4), with no test tying metrics to a single moving outcome.

expectations.text: Requires one funnel vocabulary to be chosen and kept - either Orbit's explorer / participant / contributor / advocate ladder or the casual / regular / core split, never both in the same sheet
expectations.evidence: The transcript explicitly does the opposite: "Recommendation: keep both, never merge them," and even proposes a combined 4×3 cross-tab grid mixing both vocabularies on one sheet.

expectations.text: States that two vocabularies in one sheet make every cohort definition ambiguous
expectations.evidence: The transcript argues the opposite — that the two vocabularies "measure two different axes" and keeping both is a feature, not an ambiguity: "A 'core' user... can be a pure 'explorer'... that's a real, useful signal, not a naming collision."

expectations.text: Notes that the Orbit model is no longer actively developed and cites it as a stable published framework rather than a live standard
expectations.evidence: The transcript uses 'Orbit tiers' and Discourse trust levels without any mention of the Orbit model's development status (e.g. "Behavioral definition of the Orbit tiers" section 2 has no such caveat).

expectations.text: Proposes the code-centric starter set: time to first response, change request closure ratio, contributor absence factor and release frequency
expectations.evidence: The starred starter metrics are Self-resolution rate, Feedback-to-ship ratio, First-time contributors/month, External content count/month, Contributor cohort retention, and Weekly unique actors — none of 'change request closure ratio', 'contributor absence factor', or 'release frequency' appear anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Adds a recommendability survey item as the fifth starter metric, asked roughly twice a year
expectations.evidence: No survey or recommendability (NPS-style) metric appears anywhere in the transcript; the starter scorecard is defined as exactly six numbers, all derived from GitHub/Discourse API data, not surveys.

expectations.text: Marks metrics with no prior readings as "baselining" rather than inventing a threshold for them
expectations.evidence: Section 5 instead invents numeric thresholds outright: "Self-resolution rate | >50% | 25–50% | <25%" etc., merely caveated as "starting guesses... not benchmarks" rather than being withheld pending baseline data.

expectations.text: States that at least three prior periods are needed before setting a threshold from the trailing median
expectations.evidence: No such requirement or trailing-median methodology is mentioned; section 5 just says to "recalibrate after your first baseline" with no minimum period count specified.

expectations.text: Tracks first-pull-request merge rate and time-to-merge for external contributors separately from maintainers' own pull requests
expectations.evidence: The transcript's PR metrics ('First-time contributors/month', 'Time-to-first-review', 'PR merge rate') are not split between external contributors and maintainers — e.g. 'PR merge rate | merged / (merged + closed-unmerged) | GitHub API' has no external/maintainer breakdown.
